credentials.description: Bictorys private API key sent as X-API-Key on this endpoint; sandbox and production keys differ

parameters.name: payment_type
parameters.description: The type parameter allows to select the payout service provider. E.g mtn_money, orange_money, wave_money, move_money

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: The value of this query parameter guarantees the idempotence of the operation. Several HTTP requests with the same request identified value are interpreted as the same request to be executed only once. This value may be generated randomly by the caller, but the same value should be used in case of retry.

parameters.name: X-Amzn-Trace-Id
parameters.description: The parameter Identifies this HTTP request across all services. It helps to diagnostic request errors. The parameter is added automatically by the API gateway

example_prompt: Send money to a mobile money account (Wave, Orange Money, MTN Money, etc.) as a single payout.

amount.description: Amount to send. Integer only — no decimals.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the recipient. Example: "SN", "CI", "ML", "TG", "BJ", "BF".

customerId.description: Existing customer UUID. Takes precedence over customerObject when provided.

customerObject.description: Recipient details. Required unless customerId is provided.

phone.description: Recipient mobile number as a string with + and country code prefix, no spaces. Example: "+221771234567" for Senegal.

transactionType.description: Purpose of the payout. Use "payment" for standard disbursements.

paymentReason.description: Message displayed on the recipient's receipt explaining the transfer.

merchantReference.description: Your unique internal reference for this payout.

merchant.description: Merchant authorization. Required when your account has a secretCode configured.

secretCode.description: 4-digit operator-issued merchant PIN (e.g. Orange Money or MTN merchant code) registered in Bictorys Dashboard → Entreprise → Préférences. Pass as an integer, not a string.

response_schema.description: The createPayout reference documents only id in its 201 response (PayoutObject). The sandbox returns the full transaction object, whose fields, types and status values come from TransactionObjectResponse in the transactions reference (getTransactions).

id.description: Unique identifier of the payout transaction

customerId.description: Identifier of the customer who paid the transaction

address.description: Full street address, which MAY include house number, street name, Post Office Box, etc

postalCode.description: Zip code or postal code component.

locale.description: User locale, language is lower case. Country in upper case

createdAt.description: The date time that record was created in our system.

updatedAt.description: The date time that record was updated in our system.

pspName.description: The PSP, mobile money or card,  used for this transaction

paymentChannel.description: Channel used to make the payment

amount.description: This is the amount received or paid by the merchant, net of fees. Negative on a payout: money leaving the merchant account.

merchantFees.description: The fee paid by the merchant for receiving the payment.

customerFees.description: The fee paid by the customer for receiving the payment.

transactionFeeAmountTax.description: Transaction fee tax. The value is zero if tax is not applicable

currency.description: The currency associated to the amount. If you don't specify a value, we'll assume 'XOF'

merchantReference.description: reference passed by client in the request

orderType.description: Reference to the type of the payment, invoice, paymentlink, order, flat means the merchant did not create an order or an invoice or a paymentlink prior to call charges API.

orderId.description: unique Id of the order. invoiceId, orderId or paymentlinkId. This value is empty if orderType equals to flat

deviceId.description: The identifier of the device used to make the payment

originIp.description: IP address of the device that have sent the request

timestamp.description: The time and date that  the the transaction was recorded in our system. Note that this doesn't describe when payments were executed, only when they were submitted

details.description: Bictorys error code. Examples: "E400-37: Secret code is missing", "E400-38: Insufficient balance", "E400-28: Money transfer is not authorized for this merchant".

gotchas: payment_type goes in the query string: POST /pay/v1/payouts?payment_type=wave_money. The API reference does not mark it required, but the integration guide always sends it (POST {BICTORYS_API_URL}/pay/v1/payouts?payment_type={type}). The reference enum has 10 values: wave_money, orange_money, maxit, mtn_money, free_money, moov, mobicash, togocell, bictorys, card.
transactionType is required — omitting it causes a 500. Use "payment" for standard disbursements.
idempotency-key header is effectively required — a missing idempotency-key is a known cause of 500 errors. Always send a UUID per request.

merchant.secretCode is the operator-issued merchant PIN (e.g. your Orange Money or MTN merchant code) registered in Bictorys Dashboard → Entreprise → Préférences. Required when configured on your account — omitting it returns E400-37: Secret code is missing.
customerObject.phone is a string with a + and country code prefix, no spaces. Example: "+221771234567" for Senegal. Using a numeric type causes a 400 phone error.
The response amount is a negative integer — money leaving the merchant account. Use Math.abs() if displaying to the user.

status is a string, not an integer: one of succeeded, failed, cancelled, pending, processing, reversed or authorized (PaymentStatus in the transactions reference). A completed sandbox payout returns "succeeded".
Money transfer must be explicitly enabled for your merchant account. If not, Bictorys returns E400-28: Money transfer is not authorized for this merchant. Contact Bictorys support.

A 400 error mentioning "balance" means Bictorys' own float is insufficient; a 400 error mentioning "plafond" or "limit" means the recipient's mobile money account hit its own operator-side ceiling — these are distinct failure modes and neither is retryable without merchant/recipient action.
Set your HTTP client timeout to at least 30 seconds — payout processing is slower than charge creation.
Sandbox base URL is https://api.test.bictorys.com — the production URL is https://api.bictorys.com. Sandbox payouts do not send real money.
open_questions: Does the API reject a payout without payment_type? The API reference does not mark it required; the integration guide always sends it.

Is the production payout response the same transaction object? The createPayout reference documents only id; the other response fields are those the sandbox returned, typed from TransactionObjectResponse in the transactions reference.
